title: A Daily Joy to Be Alive
author: Jimmy Santiago Baca
source: Black Mesa Poems (1989) / New Directions Publishing
citation: Baca, Jimmy Santiago. 'A Daily Joy to Be Alive.' Black Mesa Poems, New Directions, 1989.

sections.heading: A Daily Joy to Be Alive (Complete Poem)

epigraph.quote: In these ruins, green shoots emerge... reminding me that life cannot be crushed by poverty, or fences, or prison stone.

paragraphs:
It is a daily joy to be alive,
to open the door and walk out into the dawn,
feeling the cool wind brush across my knuckles,
remembering the cold steel of prison bars
and the heavy clatter of iron doors.

I walk through the ruins of old beginnings,
where houses burned down
and weeds grew through the cracked concrete,
where boys once played stickball
and sirens screamed into the night.

Yet in these ruins, green shoots emerge.
A wild sunflower pushes through the asphalt,
bright yellow petals shaking in the diesel smoke,
reminding me that life cannot be crushed
by poverty, or fences, or prison stone.

I claim my name. I claim my breath.
I lift my face to the morning sun,
not as a victim, not as a broken man,
but as one who has walked through the fire
and found within his chest a daily joy to be alive.
